body:
## MCP fleet follow-up implementation (post-#1150)

Branch off latest `main` (after PR #1150 merged). Executes the disclosed follow-up backlog from PR #1150's audit trail and design doc.

### Commits

1. **Network preflight across the remaining fleet-start entrypoints + conflict debris cleanup** — three fleet-start entrypoints were missing the `dopemux-network` preflight PR #1150 already fixed for `mcp up`:
   - `scripts/ai_startup.sh`: intentionally expands cloud bootstrap from project-scoped `mcp start` to the full catalog-backed singleton fleet. It now calls the canonical `coldstart.network.ensure_docker_networks` helper before `dopemux mcp ensure --full`, because `compose.yml` declares `dopemux-network` as external.
   - `mcp_start_all_cmd` dead-fallback branch: reuses `ensure_docker_networks` before either Compose invocation.
   - `cli.py::_start_mcp_servers_with_progress`: reuses the same helper in the `dopemux init` startup path.

   Also cleaned pre-existing conflict-marker debris from four docs. Full-file review confirmed the runtime-true global-CI remediation and queued-for-merge handoff passages remain present; only duplicate conflict debris was removed.

2. **Close P22-F3** — the three formerly deferred survivor paths received concrete dispositions: Makefile PM/webhook targets are genuinely outside MCP-fleet scope; `docker/leantime/configure_bridge.sh` delegates to `dopemux mcp up --services leantime-bridge`; dead `scripts/deploy/setup/setup_dopemux.sh` was removed. Also corrected Makefile's `webhook_receiver` service typo to the actual `webhook-receiver` Compose key.

3. **M11 rename — documented BLOCKER, not executed** — `services/task-orchestrator/**` and `services/dopecon-bridge/**` are hard-blocked by `DCP-RED-MERGE-SEAM-0001`. A partial rename would create an inconsistent split identity, so no rename subset was applied. See `claudedocs/m11-red-lane-blocker-2026-07-29.md` and the consumer sweep.

### Supervisor repair on current head

Head `8e2a60221110164e1b180f15b2ec2848ca55ddba` adds the explicit cloud-startup network preflight and `tests/unit/test_ai_startup_network_preflight.py`, which pins helper presence and ordering before full-fleet remediation.

### Explicitly out of scope

P-24 ADR implementation remains `proposed` and requires supervisor/operator acceptance before code changes.

### Current-head validation

- Local `bash -n scripts/ai_startup.sh`: **PASS**.
- Local network-helper ordering assertion: **PASS**.
- GitHub current-head unit tests: **PASS**.
- DCP red-lane gate: **PASS**.
- Code quality/lint, docs, preflight, clobber guard, repo identity, security workflow, extractor smoke, model-routing consistency, auditor-router gate, and proof validator: **PASS**.
- Complete CI pipeline: **IN_PROGRESS** at last harvest because Extractor Full had not completed.
- Independent embedded audit: **NEEDS_SUPERVISOR / FAIL-CLOSED**. The trusted audit checkout at base `72af781e42e0702d9047946e0f5a250e7dff0fa5` does not contain `scripts/audit/pal_clink_runner.py`, so no model audit executed and no passing proof could be emitted.
- PR Steward / final readiness: **NOT READY**, correctly red because the independent audit did not pass.

The previous 1743-test result belongs to the older head and is not used as current-head readiness proof.

This PR remains draft. Do not mark ready or merge until the current-head CI pipeline completes, an approved independent audit returns `PASS` or non-blocking `PASS_WITH_RISKS`, and PR Steward reports `READY` against the same head.

🤖 Generated with Claude Code; supervisor repair applied through the GitHub connector.

Three fleet-start entrypoints were missing the dopemux-network preflight
that mcp_up_cmd already had fixed in PR #1150 - same class of 'network
not found on a clean host' bug, now closed everywhere the fleet can be
bootstrapped from:

- scripts/ai_startup.sh: bare 'dopemux mcp start' only manages
  project-scoped conport/dope-memory/task-orchestrator, leaving the

- mcp_start_all_cmd's fallback (scripts/start-all.sh does not exist, so
  this branch always runs) now calls the existing
  coldstart.network.ensure_docker_networks helper before both compose
  invocations, reusing the same helper mcp_up_cmd already uses rather
  than duplicating the check-then-create logic.
- src/dopemux/cli.py::_start_mcp_servers_with_progress (the dopemux init
  default startup path, tracked as P22-F2 structural bypass) gets the
  same network-ensure preflight. This does NOT resolve P22-F2's broader
  disclosed gap (instance-overlay materialization, multi-part compose
  resolution, progress UI, post-start gate remain undelegated - that
  call remains correct per the prior audit's risk assessment) - just
  closes the specific, isolated network bug this path shares with the
  others.

Also cleaned up pre-existing, unrelated conflict-marker debris (stray
<<<<<<</=======/>>>>>>> fragments from a botched merge/rebase months
before PR #1150, confirmed unrelated by an independent audit - AGY
finding R2) in four docs: docs/pr_merge/usage-patterns.md,

docs/planes/pm/write-boundaries.md,
docs/02-how-to/pr-merge-flight-dashboard.md. Resolved by keeping the

Copied claudedocs/m11-workflow-api-rename-consumer-sweep-2026-07-29.md

commits.messageBody:
Investigation (independent Sonnet agent) found the three P22-F3 paths
were never homogeneous - they split into three different dispositions,
now each closed on its own merits:

1. Makefile pm-up/pm-down/pm-logs (leantime + mysql_leantime +
   redis_leantime) and webhook-up/down/logs/db-* (webhook-receiver):
   GENUINELY OUT OF MCP-FLEET SCOPE. Neither Leantime's own PM-app
   DB/cache nor the webhook sidecar are MCP fleet services (not in
   DEFAULT_MCP_SERVICES). Guard-test allowlist entry rewritten from a
   deferral ('flagged for a follow-up packet') to an affirmative
   justification with file:line evidence - no code change needed.

   Incidental bug found and fixed while here: the webhook-up/down/logs/
   db-* targets referenced compose service 'webhook_receiver' (underscore);
   the actual compose.yml service key is 'webhook-receiver' (hyphen) -
   every one of these targets would have failed with 'no such service'.

2. docker/leantime/configure_bridge.sh: WAS a raw fleet-service bypass
   (leantime-bridge is in DEFAULT_MCP_SERVICES). Fixed to delegate to
   the canonical `dopemux mcp up --services leantime-bridge`. Compose
   already recreates the container on the API-key config-hash change,
   so this matches the prior --force-recreate behavior for this use case
   without needing a new CLI flag. Allowlist entry removed - no raw
   compose invocation remains at this path. (Comment wording deliberately
   avoids a literal contiguous compose-up phrase so the guard regex
   doesn't flag its own explanation - same self-reference issue the
   cli.py NOTE block hit earlier in this PR.)

3. scripts/deploy/setup/setup_dopemux.sh: dead code. Zero live callers
   found (grep across .sh/.py/.md/Makefile); referenced a nonexistent
   scripts/install_claude_code_router.sh, used a doubly-nested cd path
   that doesn't exist, and invoked MCP tool names (mcp__conport__*,
   mcp__dope-context__*) as if they were shell commands - this script
   could not have run successfully in a long time. Deleted rather than
   rewritten (P-22's own disposition for genuinely dead legacy scripts).
   Allowlist entry removed.

Guard-test top docstring's P22-F3 bucket rewritten to record the closure
and the split disposition, so a future reader doesn't see a stale
'flagged for follow-up' claim for paths that are already resolved.

Tests: 83 passed (tests/mcp/ incl. all 5 guard-test functions, plus the
broader mcp_commands/cli_startup/integration suites unaffected).

Note: this amends the immediately-preceding commit on this branch, made
earlier in this same turn and not yet pushed - its message got corrupted
by unrelated docker build output bleeding into the terminal from a
concurrent process elsewhere in this shared environment, and two of its
four intended files failed to stage due to a pathspec error on the
already-git-rm'd setup_dopemux.sh path in the same `git add` invocation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: fix(mcp): close P22-F3 - resolve the three pre-existing survivor paths

commits.messageBody:
Attempted the M11 bounded rename packet (task-orchestrator FastAPI :8000
-> dopemux-workflow-api). services/task-orchestrator/app/main.py edits
were hard-blocked by the PreToolUse dcp_surface_guard.py hook -
services/task-orchestrator/** and services/dopecon-bridge/** are
DCP-RED-MERGE-SEAM-0001 red-lane paths (confirmed programmatically
against dopemux.dcp.red_lane_rules.FORBIDDEN_PATHS).

Did NOT attempt a partial rename (compose.yml/registry.yaml identifiers
changed while the service's own SERVICE_NAME/health-payload/metrics
prefixes stay 'task-orchestrator' internally) - that would produce a
THIRD, worse naming inconsistency, not a partial improvement. The M11
spec itself requires one bounded packet; splitting it across the
red-lane boundary defeats that requirement rather than working around
it.

Full blocker analysis + recommended next steps (canonical-writer
session / narrow the red lane / defer) in
claudedocs/m11-red-lane-blocker-2026-07-29.md. Recommendation: defer -
this is a hygiene rename, not a live bug; every consumer already has
working env-var-overridable defaults, and PR #1150's repair rounds
already added ':8000 is not the MCP surface' disclaimers everywhere
a reader would encounter the confusion.

The consumer-sweep evidence (claudedocs/m11-workflow-api-rename-
consumer-sweep-2026-07-29.md, committed in this branch's first batch)
remains valid for whenever this unblocks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
